{"id": "73:20/q04", "question": "What does God's measuring of night and day convey?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "73:20/q04/p1", "position": "God knows and determines the precise measures of night and day.", "reasons": "TABRISI, d. 548 (author): God apportions night and day so people can act during them as commanded. RAZI-FULL, d. 606 (author): Only God knows the exact measures of the divisions of night and day. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 (ابن العربي): Ibn al-ʿArabī says created measure itself carries no ruling; God connects to it whichever duties He wills. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 (author): God knows the exact measures of night and day, whereas people estimate through effort and may be mistaken. BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 (author): Only God knows the exact measures of night and day; placing God's name first signals exclusivity, supported by the statement that people cannot enumerate it. ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): On the genitive reading, prayer varied from night to night and people could not accurately measure the hours while sleeping; God alone knows them and eased the command to what was manageable. ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (الزمخشري): Al-Zamakhsharī says putting God's name first in the sentence expresses His exclusive control of measuring night and day; Abū Ḥayyān says exclusivity comes from context, not subject-first word order alone. SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (الزمخشري): Al-Zamakhshari says placing Allah first as subject signals that He alone determines the night. SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (author): The genitive reading describes varying prayer amounts, each below two-thirds, half, or one-third as appropriate, since sleep and human limits prevent precise measurement. IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (author): God measures the night and day so they sometimes match and sometimes one lengthens at the expense of the other. BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 (author): God alone measures night and day with exact precision and knows every minute because He created them; the verse recalls 67:14. | mentions 67:14 BURSEVI, d. 1127 (author): The fronted divine subject with the verb 'determines' makes God's exclusive ability to measure night and day emphatic. BURSEVI, d. 1127 (الراغب): Al-Raghib defines taqdīr as making the quantity of a thing clear. BURSEVI, d. 1127 (author): God alone knows the exact hours of night and day and can fulfill the right of worship in each; people can only estimate, and their effort may err. ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (author): Only God knows the precise durations and hours of night and day; placing His name as subject before yaquduru signals exclusivity, as Jar Allah argues. ELMALILI, d. 1361 (author): God alone measures and knows the true amount of night and day, and knows all time. ELMALILI, d. 1361 (author): The interpretation that the pronoun refers to God's measure of the night, adopted by al-Kashshāf and many others, is sound in itself, but can wrongly suggest the initial command was ill-judged. IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 (author): The parenthetical statement that God measures night and day fits here because He knows all the possible durations and has made them known; readings therefore do not alter the point. IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 (author): The construction subtly marks the different status and measure of the Prophet’s vigil and the group’s; 9:3 likewise distinguishes God’s disavowal from the Messenger’s public dealings with polytheists. | mentions 9:3 IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 (author): The opening statement prepares for the ensuing explanation that they cannot keep the vigil’s full measure. IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 (author): والله يقدر الليل والنهار is a parenthesis between God’s knowledge of the vigil and the statement that they cannot fully measure it; its relevance was explained above. TABATABAI, d. 1402 (author): The pronoun in lan tuhsuhu may refer to measuring night or to standing for its prescribed thirds, half, or near two-thirds. TABATABAI, d. 1402 (author): God knows because He is the creator and determiner; determining night and day entails determining their thirds, halves, and two-thirds. TABATABAI, d. 1402 (author): The verse names Allah in connection with measurement because determining measures is a matter of creation, and all creation belongs to Him. NAHHAS: God measures night and day hours. MAWARDI-FULL: God determines night and day hours for servants' acts or divine decree. WAHIDI-BASIT: God knows all night divisions and times. WAHIDI-WAJIZ: God measures night and day and their periods. DAMGHANI: Yaqduru can mean to know; God knows night and day hours. BAGHAWI-FULL: Ata says God misses no deed and knows night, day, and vigil. KASHSHAF-FULL: Only God measures night and day exactly; fronting name emphasizes exclusivity."}]}

BURSEVI, d. 1127 (author): Tāba ʿalaykum is a metaphorical extension from accepting repentance to granting a dispensation; tabʿah means the harm that follows an act. ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (author): God's turning toward them means He permits them to leave the prescribed vigil and lifts its burden; this is a metaphor comparing permission to acceptance of repentance.
